findings.face: The exposed interbrow-to-upper-nose area of face04 has skin wash and texture, but lacks a directional nasion or eye-socket-to-nose structure.
findings.nose: At alpha>=40, the nose begins at y407 and its visible range is [500,407,538,460] inclusive. In x497..540,y350..406 there are no alpha>=40 pixels; only 49 alpha>0 pixels with a maximum alpha24. Its existing shading principally describes the lower bridge, tip and nostrils.
findings.eyes: Eyes01 has only 17 alpha>0 pixels and max alpha9 in that same upper-nasion region, so its inner corner linework does not supply the missing root.
findings.brows: The three separate brow styles end at their own medial tips; the lower inner-brow-to-nose transition is not present as a continuous structure. It should not be fixed by repainting or relocating whole eyebrows.
findings.visual: The enlarged composite has a broad flat skin gap between the inner eyebrows/eyes and the nasal shading. Six combinations retain the same gap. The existing female original reference is also subtle here; an addition should remain delicate rather than copy a strongly outlined male nose.

recommended_native_redraw.layer: female nose01, as an upper transparent extension; retain independent brow/eye layers
recommended_native_redraw.coordinates: Original 1024x1536 shared canvas, x right/y down; suggested support, not mandatory opaque bounds.
recommended_native_redraw.construction: Soft paired warm skin/brown wash begins under medial brow ends, turns into the inner eye-socket slopes, narrows as it descends to the upper bridge and dissolves into the original y407..423 nose transition. Preserve a brighter central ridge instead of a continuous hard outline.
recommended_native_redraw.female_material: Lighter, softer and slightly narrower than the male nasion example, using current face04 warm skin and paper-watercolor texture.
